scope: Corollary 5.6 (Periodic inputs for boundary estimates) of the manuscript “The periodic spin-one Haldane gap” (preprints/The-periodic-spin-one-Haldane-gap-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 268 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 989f14096403897c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Xb be the spatial transfer operator of Proposition 3.1, with the shift a = 700741/500000, and put b0 = 49/4, b1 = 49/2, ℓ = 999/1000, U = 100139/100000, V = 872/1000, mJ = 1.0657205, mN = .2783155. At b = b0, the full eigenvalue list, counted with multiplicity, is the D2-invariant list J together with three identical lists N. Every eigenvalue in J has modulus less than U, and the sum of the twelfth powers of all eigenvalues in J is at most mJ . Every eigenvalue in each N list has modulus less than V , and that list’s twelfth powers sum to at most mN . There is an eigenvalue in J whose modulus exceeds ℓ. Moreover, 1 − S(72, b1) ≤ 151249 2500000 . For n = 72 and n = 120, one has E0(n) + na < 0; hence a physical ground Boltzmann factor in Zn(b) exceeds one for every b > 0.
